arml-2001-superrelay-02.title: Powers of 2
arml-2001-superrelay-02.body:
$\left(2^{24}\right)^T=(2^3)^{8T}=8^{8T}$, so the logarithm is $8T=6$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $\frac34$.)*

**Answer: 6**

arml-2001-superrelay-03.title: The $x^6$ coefficient
arml-2001-superrelay-03.body:
The product is $10x^7+5(T-2N)x^6+\cdots$ (the $x^6$ terms come from $x^2\cdot Tx\cdot5x^3$ and $(-Nx)\cdot2x^2\cdot5x^3$). Since $P$ has degree $5$, this coefficient is $0$: $T=2N$, so $\dfrac NT=\dfrac12$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $6$.)*

**Answer: $\dfrac12$**

arml-2001-superrelay-04.title: Arc lengths add
arml-2001-superrelay-04.body:
Let the diameters of the three smaller arcs be $a,b,c$; they add to the diameter $2T$ of the big one. The perimeter (the four arcs) is $\dfrac\pi2(2T+a+b+c)=\dfrac\pi2(2T+2T)=2\pi T=\pi$, so $\dfrac P\pi=1$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $\frac12$.)*

**Answer: 1**

arml-2001-superrelay-05.title: Two ways to get the area
arml-2001-superrelay-05.body:
With $BC=2$, the altitude from $A$ is $\sqrt{25-1}=2\sqrt6$ and the area is $2\sqrt6$. Also the area is $\frac12\cdot5\cdot5\sin\angle BAC$. So $\sin\angle BAC=\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{25}$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $1$.)*

**Answer: $\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{25}$**

arml-2001-superrelay-06.title: Intercepts
arml-2001-superrelay-06.body:
$K=4\sqrt6$. The line $y=K-Kx$ meets the $x$-axis at $(1,0)$ and the $y$-axis at $(0,K)$, so the area is $\frac12\cdot1\cdot K=\dfrac K2=2\sqrt6$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $\frac{4\sqrt6}{25}$.)*

**Answer: $2\sqrt6$**

arml-2001-superrelay-07.title: Inequality
arml-2001-superrelay-07.body:
$K=24-4=20$. $a_{2K}=a_K+Kd=2001+20d<2500$ gives $d<24.95$, so the largest integer is $d=24$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $2\sqrt6$.)*

**Answer: 24**

arml-2001-superrelay-08.title: Count factors of 5
arml-2001-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the relay, the two numbers received were the answers to problems 7 and 9 of the two halves of the relay: $24$ and $50$.)*

$s_3=ab$, $s_4=ab^2$, $s_5=a^2b^2$, $s_6=a^2b^3$, so $s_{2t+1}=a^tb^t$ and $s_{2t+2}=a^tb^{t+1}$. With $a=2^3\cdot3$ and $b=2\cdot5^2$ there are plenty of $2$'s, so we need $5^{2001}\mid s_k$. The exponent of $5$ in $s_{2t+1}$ is $2t$ (need $t\ge1001$, $k=2003$) and in $s_{2t+2}$ is $2t+2$ (need $t\ge1000$, $k=2002$). The power of $2$ in $s_{2002}=a^{1000}b^{1001}$ is $3000+1001\ge2001$ too. So the smallest $k$ is $2002$.

**Answer: 2002**

arml-2001-superrelay-09.title: Period 4
arml-2001-superrelay-09.body:
Subtracting the equations for $x$ and $x+1$ gives $f(x)=f(x+4)$, so $f$ has period $4$. Then $1776\equiv0$, $222\equiv2$, $1999\equiv3$, $2001\equiv1\pmod 4$, so $f(1776)+f(2001)+f(222)+f(1999)=T$: $28+f(2001)+60-83=55$, giving $f(2001)=50$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $55$.)*

**Answer: 50**

arml-2001-superrelay-10.title: Right triangle altitude
arml-2001-superrelay-10.body:
$K=5$. In right triangle $ABC$ (right angle at $B$) with altitude $BD$, $AB^2=AD\cdot AC=25\cdot(25+96)=25\cdot121$, so $AB=5\cdot11=55$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $3$.)*

**Answer: 55**

arml-2001-superrelay-11.title: Combine logarithms
arml-2001-superrelay-11.body:
$75T=135$. On the right, $2+\log_b3+\log_b5=\log_b(15b^2)$, so $135=15b^2$, $b^2=9$, $b=3$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $\frac95$.)*

**Answer: 3**

arml-2001-superrelay-12.title: Area ratio
arml-2001-superrelay-12.body:
$K=3+10=13$. $RB=Kx$, so $[ABR]=\frac12\cdot90\cdot Kx=45Kx$. This equals $\dfrac K{100}\cdot90^2=81K$, so $x=\dfrac{81}{45}=\dfrac95$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $\frac3{10}$.)*

**Answer: $\dfrac95=1.8$**

arml-2001-superrelay-13.title: Complement
arml-2001-superrelay-13.body:
$K=8+8+9=25$. The probability that both are men is $\dfrac{21}{25}\cdot\dfrac{20}{24}=\dfrac{7}{10}$, so the probability that at least one is a woman is $\dfrac3{10}$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $889$.)*

**Answer: $\dfrac3{10}$**

arml-2001-superrelay-14.title: Inequality
arml-2001-superrelay-14.body:
$a_{K+9}=2001+9d>10000$ gives $9d>7999$, $d>888.\overline8$, so the least integer is $889$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $60$ and $K=\frac T3=20$; the value of $K$ is not needed.)*

**Answer: 889**

arml-2001-superrelay-15.title: Count
arml-2001-superrelay-15.body:
The one-digit primes are $2,3,5,7$. There are $4^3=64$ three-digit numbers with all digits prime; remove the four with all digits equal ($222,333,555,777$): $60$.

**Answer: 60**
